newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Somerfield eyes margin rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Somerfield eyes margin rise.

text.p: British neighbourhood supermarket group Somerfield Plc continues to see improvements in operating margin and is still targeting four to five percent levels, chief executive David Simons said on Thursday.
"The current year has started well and operating margins continue to improve," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Somerfield improved operating margins to 3.6 percent in the year ending April 26 from 3.2 percent a year earlier as it saw pretax profits rise to 105.4 million pounds from a pro-forma 92 million before its float in August 1996.
"We expect operating margins to improve to between say four and five percent...but we haven't put timescales on when we would achieve that," Simons added.

Simons said that operating margins in the full-year were helped by a one percentage point rise in gross margin helped by an improved product mix, an emphasis on fresh foods and own label and better support from suppliers for promotional campaigns.
Around 60 percent of that gain was invested in loyalty schemes, supply chain improvements, training and marketing, Simons said.
Simons pointed out that the Somerfield fascia stores had seen an improvement in volumes to 2.8 percent in the first eight weeks of the current year from 2.2 percent last year.
But food prices are currently decreasing by 1.4 percent currently compared with inflation of 1.8 percent in the year to April 26.
Simons said he saw consumer demand for food currently "relatively steady. It is not euphoric by any stretch of the imagination but we are seeing steady growth."
He said the company aimed to invest some 130-140 million pounds this year, up from 104 million last year.
Somerfield will be opening seven new stores this year but Simons said he saw most of the anticipated growth in sales from improvement in volumes and operating margins at its existing 600 stores.
Simons said the company aimed to "complement rather than compete" with large, out-of-town superstores with its largely local, neighbourhood locations.

"We have a very clear customer base which is actually quite different from the out-of-town superstore," Simons said, adding that Somerfield attracted top-up shoppers and those who do their main shop in more than one visit.
Somerfield also had primary customers who might not want to go to out-of-town stores because it is too big, too inconvenient to reach or too impersonal, he said. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
